findings.title: Change dates is only reachable through an unlabelled three-dot menu on the berth list
findings.description: On the choose-berth page the stay summary ("Arriving on … at …, staying …") is plain text and there is no visible date control or "Change" link. The only route to change dates is the icon-only "More options" button (three dots), whose menu contains "Change dates". Skippers who want to move their arrival by a day do not associate a three-dot icon with dates.
findings.impact: Skippers abandon the berth list, restart the booking or phone the office to change a date — a core task in PRODUCT.md.
findings.recommendation: Put a visible "Change dates" link next to the stay summary on the berth list; keep the menu item if wanted.

findings.title: The "Booking stopped / BK-409" state gives no reason, no next step and no way back

criteria.name: Every stop in the booking says what to do next

findings.description: When the entered length exceeds the chosen berth's limit, the boat form is hidden and replaced by "Booking stopped" and "This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409." There is no explanation that the boat is too long for the berth, no suggestion of a berth that fits, no link back to the berth list, and the typed details are not kept.
findings.impact: Skippers cannot recover inside the booking; they close the browser, restart and retype, or phone the office.
findings.recommendation: Say in plain words that the boat (length X m) is longer than the berth limit (Y m), offer the berths that fit with a link back to the list, and keep the typed boat details.

findings.title: Tide table is in UTC while arrival times are local, with no conversion or warning
findings.description: The tide table caption reads "High water at the quay, times in UTC" while the arrival-time select and the rest of the booking use local clock time (BST in October until the 25th). Nothing converts the times or warns that they differ by an hour, so skippers matching their arrival to high water read the table as local time.
findings.impact: Skippers arrive an hour off the sill-gate window and wait outside or miss the gate — a safety-relevant fact per PRODUCT.md.
findings.recommendation: Show tide times in local time (BST/GMT as applicable) and label the zone; keep UTC only as a secondary column if passage planners want it.

findings.title: Arrival-time list offers and accepts times when the sill gate is closed, with no warning

criteria.name: Show the tide window wherever a time is chosen

findings.description: The arrival-time select lists every hour from 06:00 to 21:00 regardless of the chosen date. The gate is open only about two hours either side of high water, but choosing e.g. 10:00 on 17 October (HW 14:32 UTC) and pressing "Check berths" proceeds with no warning and no display of the gate window next to the field.
findings.impact: Skippers book an arrival they cannot make and only find out at the harbour entrance.
findings.recommendation: Show the gate window for the chosen date next to the time field and either limit the list to times inside it or warn before continuing.

findings.title: Boat "Length" field states no unit, unlike "Draught in metres"
findings.description: The Length label gives no unit; the neighbouring Draught field says "in metres". Any positive number is accepted, so a length in feet (e.g. 34) passes validation and then ends at the unexplained BK-409 stop because it exceeds every berth limit.
findings.impact: Skippers who think in feet enter feet and hit a dead end, or have to guess the unit.
findings.recommendation: Put "in metres" in the label and flag implausible values (for example over 15) with "Enter the length in metres".

findings.title: Booking pages show no step count or progress
findings.description: None of the four booking pages (plan, berth, boat, review) shows "Step n of 4" or similar. Verifier should confirm the absence on each.
findings.impact: Skippers on poor signal cannot judge whether they will finish before losing coverage.
findings.recommendation: Add "Step n of 4" above each h1.

findings.title: Booking pages reported slow or timing out on weak mobile data
findings.description: Three reporters say the booking site was slow or timed out on 4G at sea (one had no signal at all). Verifier should check page weight, request count and render-blocking resources under a throttled network; field conditions cannot be reproduced locally.
findings.recommendation: Only if measurement shows weight or blocking resources: inline critical CSS and keep pages small.

evidence.detail: theme TH-13-slow-on-weak-signal; prevalence pooled 3/94 people; by channel tickets 1/36, survey 1/34, reviews 1/24

factor_notes.frequency: tickets: 1 of 36 people; survey: 1 of 34 people; reviews: 1 of 24 people (self-selected channels count reporters, not users)

verification_check.reason: The claim is about performance on weak mobile data in the field. uie probe cannot throttle the network, and the candidate itself says field conditions cannot be reproduced locally. On the unthrottled local server, / loaded in 19 ms, the berths, boat and review pages each completed goto in about 0.5 s, and there were no failed or 4xx/5xx requests. That neither confirms nor refutes the claim. It needs a throttled measurement (Lighthouse or DevTools Slow 4G: page weight, request count, render-blocking resources) or field data from a human.
